grade.first_issue: The intersecting-family lemma is applied without handling the cases \(|N^c(v)|=0\), or \(|N^c(v)|=1\) when its sole flag set may be empty; the lemma as stated is not valid in those cases.
grade.summary: The graph construction, clique observation, frequency bound, and final algebra are correct and establish the stronger conclusion \(\omega\ge204\) whenever the lemma applies. The omitted exceptional cases are repaired directly: if \(|N^c(v)|\le1\), then \(|N(v)|\ge2022\), so \(5(\omega-1)\ge2022\), already implying \(\omega\ge406\).
strengths: Correctly translates the triple condition into \(\alpha(G)\le2\) and proves that every non-neighborhood is a clique.
Provides a valid pigeonhole argument for nontrivial pairwise-intersecting families.
Correctly combines the neighborhood and non-neighborhood bounds to obtain a stronger result.

errors.description: The lemma’s edge cases are omitted, so the displayed inequality for \(\omega\) is not justified for every chosen vertex as written.
